question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. If $A$ is symmetric, then ${A}^{2}$ is always symmetric.

II. The sum of *any* two $n\times n$ matrices is always symmetric.

III. If $A$ is *any*  $n\times n$ matrix, then $A+{A}^{T}$ is always symmetric.
question.worked_solution:
A square matrix $A$ is symmetric if it is equal to its transpose:

$$
A={A}^{T}
$$

Equivalently, ${a}_{ij}={a}_{ji}$ for all $i,j.$ In other words, $A$ is symmetric across its main diagonal.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, for any symmetric matrix $A,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}(AA)^{T} & ={A}^{T}{A}^{T} \\  & =AA.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is false. As a counterexample, consider the matrices 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$ 

However, their sum is not symmetric:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, for any square matrix $A,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}(A+{A}^{T})^{T} & ={A}^{T}+({A}^{T})^{T} \\  & ={A}^{T}+A \\  & =A+{A}^{T}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
